item.title: Unit 1 : What is Information
item.description:
This blog is to traverse through the ideologies of what do you mean by Information. The first unit we covered was _‘What is Information’_which is one of the most intresting thing I came across. In this unit we mainly covered “DIKW also known as the Data Knowledge Wisdom model”. At begning this felt more intuitive as this depicts the linear flow of information that is raw data which is gradually transformed into complex structures. The simplicity made me understand the progression but tranisition from knowledge wisdom was often blurry. Data was raw facts which then organised to form Information, knowldge comes from identifying these patterns, whereas wisdom is making decision based on our understanding.

However as I started applying and questioning whether this is applicable on everyday processes. I soon understood this isn’t the case as knowledge does not simly emerge from filtering out the information or by breaking down the comple task into a organised structure. As most of time, learning is not linear. Most of the time knowledge influence how we intrepret data, therefore we cannot strictly say that it upward flow from data to wisdom.

I also found it quite amusing that this model is about simpler linear learning but in reality how we understand anything is much more complex which involves a lot processes like mistakes, intuition, intrepretation. In addition we know human has a limitation of how much information or how many variables which can be processed at a time. Therefore it is challenging if we put constraints or follow certain model or representation for process information or any data. Another point inorder make it more conveyable data visualisation plays an important role. Effective vislualisation makes patterns clear and help intrepretation of any data way easier if it it simplified. As we discussed in class this also wide spectrum where we dealt with a lot of complex graphs which made it hard for us to ever make a point what is being presented. On the other there were lot of graphs which were presented with the users o mind.

In my opinion by combining all of the ideas we covered in Unit 1, it is always important to keep in mind about the targeted audience while making anything. Making sense of data not always follow a linear attern it also means understanding it and also representing it which is understandable by human or the congnitive limit of us.

item.title: UNIT 2 : Nature Of Image Transformation
item.description:
Personally what stood out for me in this particular unit was that information problems are not only working with data but also making small manipulation to get a better understanding. Topic like image transformation involves a lot of choices which hugely impact the outcome.  Image manipulation was easier to connect as we had a template to work with and visualise flipping it or adjusting brightness by bringing changes in the pixels. This made me realise how information is represented and whether changes are reversible or associative.  Transformation of images was most easiest for me and also at the same time hard as it had lot of mathematical aspects which is required for it. But at the same with help of these tools it will make the life easier by applying them on function which act as real life filters by either increasing contrast, flipping the image, inverting the images. Personally I found optimisation to be interesting yet hard as it connected towards  finding the best solution but the methods were abstract. But I realised what is the “best” depends on how we choose the conditions. But these optimisation are something which wired into our brain that we regularly use in our day to day life. For example finding the best route based on our needs like least time, with more restaurants etc. Other would be budgeting were we set a value for each item to have a minimum amount to be spend.

Modeling and abstraction are a bit challenging as it requires not of understanding of the targeted audience. For example in case of the elevator we need a simlyified example but at the same not oversimplification that it becomes unrealistic. The way we present our data depends on the target audience(how much pre-requistic knowledge they have).

Summarising of the unit in three points :

  • Representation of the problem -Abstraction and modeling of the data or any problem for better understanding.
  • Transformation - of the data by applying many filters.
  • Evaluation - that is optimisation finding if the give solution is the best outcome

item.title: Unit 3 : Reflecting on Failure
item.description:
Failure, was always something which was avoided or hidden due to it’s association with it being a negative aspect. I tended to see it as something which was caused due to my own fault at a personal level. For example, while exams, I blamed myself for not performing well, beating myself for being incompetent. But the thing I ignored was the effort I have given for understanding the concept irrespective of the exam. This reshaping in thinking was due to this particular unit. This course, has significantly impacted me to push myself to develop critical thinking to reduce errors but also develop ways to process them too.

The book Right Kind of Wrong and the case studies helped me to categorise and understand failure in a whole new way. It gave me a clear distinction of basic, complex, intellectual failures which helped to to have strategised approach for solving errors I face. In the case study the situation an error became a failure due to ignorance of various warnings. The presentation approach helped because it helped us to move beyond surface-level explanation and started analysing the patterns, assumptions, and causes. What helped me particularly was connecting this to my own experience by trying to classify errors and evaluating of how it can prevented. For example, I missed the reflection blog submission deadline but instead of ignoring the error which was caused due to disorganisation, I created a todo list with active reminder to make sure it wouldn’t repeated. Therefore, it comes down to how these ideologies are implemented into our life. Overall, this course really helped by changing my perspective on failures or more precisely how I deal with them.
